items.title: Steering relay rod fatigue crack
items.summary: Repeated full-lock steering under high effort can crack the steering relay rod.

tsbs.title: 3VZ-E V6 head gasket — Special Service Campaign V06
tsbs.summary: Head gasket replacement for 3VZ-E trucks built 1/90–10/94; replaced a 1996 policy adjustment and expired 24 September 2018.

timeline.change: All-new steel body on the Hilux frame; coil-sprung four-link rear axle; 22R-E or 3VZ-E; rear-wheel ABS standard on SR5 V6
V6 trucks built 1/90–10/94 fall in Toyota's head-gasket campaign window; ask for proof of the gasket job
Facelift: one-piece front bumper, modular headlamps, new interior trim; US two-door sales end August 1992
Two-door production ends May 1993; Japan's Hilux Surf gains the 1KZ-TE 3.0 turbo-diesel (August)
Side-impact door beams added for the US
Final year; keeps door beams; replaced by the Prado-based 1996 4Runner

identify.intro: The 2nd gen shares its nose, front suspension and engines with the 1989–95 Hilux, and rare two-doors and Japanese Surfs muddy the water.

items.head: Two-door
items.body: Built from launch to May 1993 (US sales ended August 1992, Canada through 1993). Toyota priced them above the four-door because of the chicken tax, so they are genuinely rare.

items.head: Pre- or post-facelift
items.body: 1990–91 trucks have rectangular sealed-beam headlamps; the 1992-on facelift brought one-piece bumpers and modular headlamps.

items.head: Engine and transfer case
items.body: V6 (3VZ-E) trucks got a chain-driven transfer case; four-cylinder (22R-E) trucks kept the older gear-driven case.

items.head: Model codes
items.body: Toyota coded V6 trucks VZN130 and diesel trucks LN130/KZN130; the diesel, wide-body and limited-slip versions were Japanese or European, not US-market 4Runners.

values.intro: Still the cheapest way into an old 4Runner, but clean V6 five-speed SR5s now pull well above the pack.
values.note: Based on 22 Bring a Trailer sales from May to October 2026 (median about $11,750). The top sale was a 1993 SR5 V6 five-speed at $36,250.

paragraphs: Japan's Hilux Surf (N120/N130) came with diesels the US never got: the 2L-TE, 3L and, from August 1993, the 3.0 1KZ-TE turbo-diesel, plus wide-body trims. All are now older than 25 years, so they can be imported without meeting US federal safety standards, but they are right-hand drive and state titling and emissions rules still apply.

production.intro: Built at Tahara, Japan (and by a joint venture in China), from 1989 to August 1995.

items.k: US sales (calendar year; 1989 sales are listed on the 1st gen, 1995 includes early 3rd gens)
